text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Namibia's deputy ombudsman, Ephraim Kasuto, who was unconstitutionally appointed chief ombudsman last year and later lost out when proper proceedings were followed, has instructed lawyers over the withdrawal of his initial appointment. The Namibian Press Agency reported this week that the government could face a N$2 million lawsuit for the alleged humiliation he suffered.

- The leadership of the Epupa Himba community and the Supreme Council of Okaoko have reiterated their objections against the planned Epupa hydro electric power scheme. The project, which is currently studied, would involve the building of a dam at Epupa in northwest Namibia.

- The government said Gendor, Atlantic Sea Products, Glomar Fisheries, Continental Fisheries and Consortium Fisheries had been awarded exploitation rights for deepwater fishing off Namibia's coast. Continental and Consoritum Fisheries will only be allocated quotas next year. The other three companies will be able to start fishing in April.
